decision: CORRECTIVE to D002, which the methodology reviewer FAILED. I accept the FAIL and WITHDRAW, in full, the pre-committed decision rule in D002 that read 'if the re-derived action sequence is identical in 20/20 trials and the route-intention disagreement rate is 0, I will record H8/H5a as VACUOUS-not-falsified'. That clause is void and will not be executed. Replacement: the F9-C1 re-aggregation (already completed by the statistician, results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json + _memo.md) stands as a purely EXPLORATORY measurement with NO status consequence for any hypothesis. H5 and H3 remain 'untested'. H8 and H5a receive no status at all, because registry/hypotheses.json lists them under proposed_loop1 as 'PROPOSALS ONLY - not registered hypotheses' and an object with no status cannot undergo a status transition. No new status label is created: 'VACUOUS-not-falsified' is not in status_labels ['untested','supported','falsified','inconclusive','needs replication'] and I am not adding it. Additionally adopted from the review: the tie-break for the re-aggregation is HOLD with tie_broken and the full vote vector logged (critiques/loop1_auditor.md:281-282), which is what makes 'identical in 20/20' well-defined; and the citation for the legacy disagreement field is corrected to falsify/org.py:161, not :160. The re-aggregation's decision-relevance is preserved WITHOUT any status claim: a measured zero means I decline to spend the 3-4h aggregation-rule build, which is a resource-allocation call fully inside L1, not a verdict about a hypothesis.
reason: The reviewer's three substantive blockers are correct on the documents and I do not contest any of them. (1) H8/H5a are proposals, not registered hypotheses, so my clause presupposed an object that does not exist in the registry; actually creating it would be registering a split of registered H5, which AUTHORITY.md makes Level 2. (2) 'VACUOUS-not-falsified' is outside status_labels, and adding a label is a registry amendment, not an L1 status update. (3) Most importantly, AUTHORITY.md L1 permits a status update only 'when PREREGISTERED criteria are met', and my criteria were written inside the very decision that would consume them, which is precisely the post-hoc pattern the reviewer exists to catch; that I wrote them before seeing the numbers does not make them preregistered. The reviewer also correctly notes H8's own prediction is CONDITIONAL on a non-zero disagreement rate, so an unmet antecedent already yields 'untested' under the existing vocabulary and I never needed a new label. I note for the record that the reviewer's fourth blocker ('results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json does not exist and no timeline entry follows') was a race condition: the statistician wrote the file at 12:10 and the memo at 12:12, after the reviewer's filesystem check. data/trials/ is confirmed unmodified by the reviewer, so the read-only commitment held. I am not contesting the FAIL on that basis; the three authority findings are sufficient on their own and the clause is withdrawn regardless.
alternatives_rejected: Contest the FAIL and keep the clause: refused outright. AUTHORITY.md states the reviewer's FAIL may not be ignored, and on the merits the reviewer is right about all three authority findings. | Escalate the clause to Level 2 and seek a reviewer PASS to register H5a/H8 and add a status label this loop: rejected as premature and as the wrong instinct. Registering a hypothesis split is a real L2 action that deserves its own argument from the scientist, not a rescue vehicle for a clause I should not have written; and the re-aggregation result does not require it, because declining to fund a 3-4h build needs no hypothesis verdict. | Discard the re-aggregation entirely as tainted by the bad clause: rejected, disproportionate. The measurement itself was ruled legitimate by the reviewer (route-intention redefinition NOT Level 2: disagreement_rounds is secondary per PREREG_V2.md:32, the token artifact is confirmed at org.py:161, and C7 specified the redefinition at loop1_auditor.md:289-290 BEFORE my decision). The defect was in the inference I pre-authorized, not in the data work, so the correct remedy is to strike the inference and keep the measurement labelled EXPLORATORY. | Record H5/H3 as 'inconclusive' instead: rejected, and this is the same error the lab already avoided in loop 1 - their IV never varied, so they were never tested at all and 'untested' is the honest label.

reviews.findings: ACCEPTED IN FULL: the withdrawal is complete, correct and correctly reasoned. D003 voids the clause, concedes all three authority findings in terms that match the documents (H8/H5a are proposals under registry/hypotheses.json proposed_loop1 with no status to transition; 'VACUOUS-not-falsified' is outside status_labels; criteria written inside the consuming decision are not preregistered), creates no status label, applies no status, leaves H3/H5 'untested', and adopts both omissions (HOLD tie-break with tie_broken logged, org.py:161). Level 1 is correct for a withdrawal: it strictly reduces the authority exercised and amends no protocol. 1. MY FOURTH BLOCKER WAS A RACE CONDITION - CORRECTION ACCEPTED AND RECORDED. results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json (mtime 12:10:59), _reaggregation.py and _memo.md (12:12:04) all exist and were written after my filesystem check. My finding 2 on D002 was factually wrong at the time I wrote it and I withdraw it. The D002 FAIL stands on the three authority findings alone, as D003 states. I have now audited the artifact: source sha256 recorded, source_mutated false, 0 model calls, _meta carries the EXPLORATORY label and no_hypothesis_status_change_proposed true, the HOLD tie-break is implemented (tie_frequency 0/80), and an adversarial sensitivity analysis over all unrecoverable role-intentions shows 0 rounds could flip. This is good work and exceeds what D002 promised. 2. THE RESOURCE-ALLOCATION CLAIM - I UPHOLD IT. Declining to fund the 3-4h aggregation-rule build on a measured 0/80 is NOT a disguised hypothesis verdict, and I attacked it on the strongest grounds I could find. The case against it: the build is the only vehicle for testing H8/H5a, so declining it forecloses the test, and recording 'the rate is zero, we will not build' carries the epistemic payload of 'inert' while shedding the label that would attract review - D003's own phrase 'decision-relevance is preserved WITHOUT any status claim' is exactly the shape of a laundered verdict. Why that fails: (a) H8's registered-as-proposed prediction is explicitly CONDITIONAL on a non-zero within-round route-intention disagreement rate, so 0/80 leaves its antecedent unmet IN THIS DATASET and says nothing about H8 in any dataset where the IV varies - a verdict would have to generalize, and this cannot; (b) the registry is untouched: H8/H5a remain unregistered proposals with no status, so the decision leaves no registry trace and retires nothing; (c) specs/AUTHORITY.md L1 explicitly includes 'choose among approved families' and sequencing of diagnostics within budget - allocation among candidate builds is the core L1 competence, and if declining to spend 3-4h required a reviewer PASS the PI could not sequence anything; (d) the alternative D003 rejected ('declare H8/H5a inert on arithmetic alone') is the actual verdict-shaped move, and it was rejected. A funding call and a verdict come apart here, and they demonstrably do. Do not strip it. 3. CONCERN - REVERSIBILITY IS NOT STATED IN D003. The declination is only distinguishable from a verdict if it is scoped to the present dataset and reversible. D002 contained that scoping ('a measured NON-zero would revive H8 as the cheapest live hypothesis in the registry'); D003, which supersedes the relevant part of D002, does not restate it. FIX: add to D003 an explicit line that the declination is scoped to exp001_pilot's 80 rounds and is reversed by any future non-zero route-intention disagreement rate, and that no downstream document may paraphrase it as H8 being inert, dead, falsified or vacuous. Without that line the distinction I just upheld is unrecorded and will not survive summarization. 4. CONCERN - THE MEASURED ZERO IS PARTLY STRUCTURAL, AND D003 DOES NOT SAY SO. The re-aggregation's own section 3 reports a measurement-validity finding that materially qualifies the number the funding decision rests on: 2 of the 4 roles (researcher, reviewer) have NO route field in their output schema (falsify/org.py SCHEMAS:20-23), so their route intention is never structurally recorded; 14/160 free-text role-rounds were unrecoverable; and the two roles that DO have structured route fields are planner and executor, who are already coupled by EDGE_CASE_POLICY sec.F planner authority. A disagreement rate measured on an instrument that cannot express the construct for half the roles is not a clean zero - it is adjacent to the sec.K floor logic the lab applied to H1. The statistician handled this honestly (adversarial imputation: 0 rounds flip; dropping both free-text roles leaves planner vs executor agreeing 80/80), which is why this is a CONCERN and not a FAIL. But D003 cites the result as a plain 'measured zero' and does not carry the qualification. FIX: state in D003 that the zero is conditional on an instrument that structurally cannot record route intention for 2 of 4 roles, and that the adversarial sensitivity analysis is what licenses relying on it. 5. CONCERN - PROVENANCE POINTS AT A FAILED DECISION. results/exp001_pilot_reaggregation.json _meta records 'authorized_by: decisions/D002.json (PI, Level 1)'. D002 has verdict FAIL. The analysis portion of D002 was and remains legitimately L1 (I ruled the route-intention redefinition not Level 2: disagreement_rounds is secondary per PREREG_V2.md:32, the artifact is confirmed at org.py:161, and C7 at loop1_auditor.md:289-290 specified the redefinition beforehand), so the artifact is not tainted. But its only authorization pointer is to a failed record. FIX: re-authorize the artifact under D003 and update _meta.authorized_by, so no future reader has to reconstruct which half of D002 survived. 6. RESIDUAL CITATION INCONSISTENCY. D003 correctly adopts org.py:161, but the artifact still carries the old reference in two places: the JSON key 'legacy_disagreement_field_org_py_160' and the memo section 2 table row 'Legacy disagreement (falsify/org.py:160)'. Verified: the expression is at falsify/org.py:161; line 160 is executor_overridden. FIX: correct both in the artifact, not only in the decision. 7. EVIDENCE - NUMBERS CHECK OUT, WITH ONE UNIT AMBIGUITY WORTH FIXING. Independently recomputed from data/trials/exp001_pilot.jsonl: legacy disagreement flags 6 role-rounds (D: 5, C: 1, C0: 0, D0: 0) = 6/80 = 0.075, matching the memo exactly; route-intention disagreement 0/80; 20/20 sequences identical. The repeated claim 'disagreement_rounds=1.0 in cell D' is CORRECT but is a per-trial COUNT (cell D per-trial values [1,2,1,1,0], mean 1.0 rounds/trial), not a proportion; as a rate it is 0.25 of rounds, which is what the memo reports. Stated bare as '1.0' it reads as 100% and has been repeated that way since timeline 11:10:03. FIX: always give the unit. 8. CONFIRMATORY vs EXPLORATORY: clean. EXPLORATORY is carried in _meta, in the memo header and in D003, and 'no_hypothesis_status_change_proposed: true' is machine-readable in the artifact. The memo's line 'I checked rather than assumed, and I did not find the interesting counter-result' is the correct register. 9. NOVELTY: none. CONFLICTS: none ignored; D003 engages every finding of review_D002.md including the one it corrects. ALTERNATIVES-REJECTED: no misrepresentation; the refusal to escalate the clause to L2 as a 'rescue vehicle for a clause I should not have written' is the right instinct and I endorse it. VERDICT CONCERNS: the corrective is accepted, the resource-allocation call is upheld, and findings 3-6 are documentation fixes that must be made before the re-aggregation is cited anywhere downstream.
